name: Weighted average across opening, purchase and sale
description: The reference case the constitution spells out. Every presented figure
below was computed by hand and appears verbatim in NON_NEGOTIABLES §3.
Implementations may change; these numbers may not. If a change to the
costing code makes this file fail, the code is wrong — not the file.
ADR-0015 changed ONE number here, and only at storage scale:
inventoryValue was 9533.3334, the result of 110 × 86.666667. That is the
recomputation rule 16 forbids. The valuation is the carried value —
13000.0000 − 3466.6667 = 9533.3333 — which is the same number the GL is
debited, so the two agree by construction. No published figure changed:

$comment: Amounts are numeric(19,4) and the average is numeric(19,6) (ADR-0011).
These are what gets stored; the values above are what gets shown.
valueOnHand and inventoryGlBalance are EQUAL, and equal by construction:
both are 13000.0000 − 3466.6667, the same stored COGS amount. That
identity is Invariant 10, and ADR-0015 makes it structural.
quantity_on_hand × average_cost. This is NOT the inventory valuation.
Rule 16 and ADR-0015 §7: no report recomputes cost. Pinned here so the
figure cannot creep back in as an expectation — a test that asserts
this number IS the valuation is the defect this entry exists to catch.
It differs from the carried value by 0.0001 at this quantity, by 0.0005
at ten times the quantity, and by zero for some splits. That is why it
cannot be accommodated with a tolerance.
A2 — sell the remaining 110 at the held average.
This is the case that shows why the recomputation is not merely
imprecise but wrong. Under ADR-0007 as written the inventory GL would
end at −0.0001 with zero stock behind it: an asset account with a
credit balance.
ADR-0015 §5: at zero quantity the inventory leg flushes the carried
value and the difference is posted to the rounding account. Quantity
and value reach zero TOGETHER, and the entry balances exactly at 4 dp.
A3 — the same scenario at ten times the quantity, as ONE transaction.
The carried value still equals the GL exactly. The recomputation is now
off by 0.0005 — five times the gap for ten times the quantity, because
the average's rounding error is per-unit and the recomputation
multiplies it by the whole quantity on hand.
This is the case that proves a tolerance can never be sized: it grows
with quantity, and a tolerance wide enough to cover it at scale is wide
enough to hide an inventory movement that never reached the GL.
A4 — ten sales of 4 against one sale of 40.
They are NOT equivalent, and that is expected behaviour rather than a
defect (ADR-0015 §9). Each of the ten roundings is independently
correct: every movement's cogs_amount is the auditable quantity ×
stored average, rounded once at boundary 2. Ten roundings simply
accumulate more than one does.
What matters is that value_on_hand equals the inventory GL balance
EXACTLY in both, because both subtract the same stored deltas.
Invariant 10 holds either way; only the path-dependent total differs.
Anyone trying to make the two paths agree is proposing to round
somewhere other than boundary 2.
